We need to decide how to resolve the March order. There are two remaining March orders for Stark: one in "the-shivering-sea" (orderId 1 March -1) with unit ID 4 (ship). The other in "white-harbor" (orderId 2 March +0) with unit ID 3 (footman). The Action Guidance gives legal reachable regions for each.

We have to choose which starting region to resolve now (starting_region_id). We only have moves for up to 1 destination (maxMoves 1). We cannot move both orders in the same action; we must choose one. We need to output JSON with starting_region_id, moves (list with possible 1 object), leave_power_token boolean.

We are in phase resolve-single-march. The system expects us to provide moves for the chosen starting region.

We should analyze options.

Potential strategic approach: keep castles and strongholds. Stark currently controls 2 castle areas: castle-black (which is region "castle-black"? Actually castle-black is a land area with castle=0? Wait "castle-black" area has no castle (castle=0). The castle areas for Stark are "winterfell" (home area has a castle? winterfell has castle=2 i.e., stronghold). And "castle-black"? The "castle-black" area is a land area with no castle? Let's verify map: "castle-black [land; crown=1]" No castle, just crown; is that a castle area? Only castle=1 (castle) or 2 (stronghold). This indicates that castle-black has no castle area. Stark's controlled castle areas: According to strategic overview, Stark has castles=2, strongholds=1. Which areas are those? Likely "winterfell" (stronghold) and "castle-black"? Actually castles: maybe "white-harbor"? White-harbor has castle=1 according to map line: "white-harbor [land; castle=1]" yes with castle=1. So Stark controls white-harbor (castle). Also "the-shivering-sea" is a sea area, no castle. The "the-shivering-sea" does not have castle. So the two castles are "winterfell" (stronghold) and "white-harbor" (castle). Also maybe "castle-black"? But that has no castle. So controlling the two castle areas is important.

Currently, "white-harbor" has a March +0 order and a footman unit (unit ID 3). The order's reachable destinations include: castle-black (land, no castle), karhold (no castle), moat-cailin (castle=1), widows-watch (no castle), winterfell (stronghold). So moving the footman from white-harbor to moat-cailin would capture a castle (moat-cailin has castle=1). That would give Stark an extra castle area. However, moving out of white-harbor would vacate it. If we vacate white-harbor and do not leave a power token, Stark would lose control of the castle area (white-harbor). So moving the footman would cause loss of white-harbor castle and potentially gain moat-cailin castle. Net result: same number of castle areas (still 2). But we need to consider supply: Stark's supply is currently 1. Let's check current supply. Observation says Stark supply = 1. They have 5 power tokens. Controlled supply icons: 1, the one at "winterfell" presumably. They have units: footman at white-harbor (unit 3), ship at the shivering sea (unit 4). That's it.

Supply level 1 permits army sizes: "1" corresponds to supply of 1 => allowed army sizes: 2,2? Actually supply track: supply=0: 2,2 ; supply=1: 3,2 . So with supply 1, Stark may have up to 2 armies: one up to 3 units, and one up to 2 units. Stark currently has a footman (single) (no army) and a ship (single) (no army). Single units don't count as army, supply doesn't restrict. But if moving footman to moat-cailin, still a single unit; no army.

If we also consider the ship in the-shivering-sea: reachable destinations list from actionGuidance: For the-shivering-sea with order -1 and unit ID 4, reachable region is only "the-narrow-sea". That is a sea area with no castle; but moving there may lead to combat? The field "triggersCombat": false. So no combat. Also ship unit can move: but moving ship away from the Shivering Sea would vacate it, but that area is a sea area (no castle). No need to leave control token. So moving ship doesn't affect castle count.

Potentially we may want to move the ship to connect with other units for future ship transport; but currently Stark has only a ship and a footman. The ship at the-shivering-sea may be used to transport footmen later to other coastal areas like Castle Black? But we need ship transport at least 2 sea areas adjacent with ship units. At the moment, Stark ship is at the-shivering-sea. It could move to the-narrow-sea. Adjacent sea areas: the-shivering-sea is adjacent to the-narrow-sea, winterfell, etc? Actually per neighbours list: the-shivering-sea neighbours: castle-black (land) via winterfell? Not sure.

However, moving the ship to the-narrow-sea might bring near White Harbor? Actually white-harbor adjacent to the-narrow-sea? The list for white-harbor at reach did not include the-narrow-sea; it's a land area. So ship transport may require a chain of ship units across sea areas. The Shivering Sea (SS) is adjacent to The Narrow Sea (TNS), White Harbor? In map: "the-shivering-sea [sea]: castle-black, karhold, the-narrow-sea, white-harbor, widows-watch, winterfell". But per actionGuidance, reachable only "the-narrow-sea" (for this March order). That's because the March order is -1; maybe includes only one movement step for the March: we cannot move to multiple destinations.

We could also choose to not move any unit at all and discard the order (empty moves) to avoid losing white-harbor castle (if we choose to resolve the white-harbor March order and leave unit, we have to vacate the area? Actually the March order is at white-harbor, but you can also choose to not move any units (empty moves) being an empty moves list discards the March order without moving anyone. That would keep the footman in place, preserving control, and discard the order.

Alternatively, we could resolve the March order for the Shivering Sea to move the ship to the-narrow-sea (no loss of castle), then later we have the white-harbor March order still present. For White Harbor we might later decide to discard or move footman.

Goal: maximize castles and strongholds, preserve supply, preserve power tokens, secure positions. Stay at net castle count.

If we move footman to moat-cailin, we gain a castle; lose white-harbor castle. Net same castle count, but we would have changed control area, maybe advantageous because Moat Cailin is central near winterfell and the Shivering Sea? Also Moat Cailin is adjacent to many areas; might be used for support later.

But we may lose ability to defend white-harbor; but white-harbor is in the north, may be vulnerable to Greyjoy or Baratheon later. Maybe we want to keep white-harbor; it's a castle region next to winterfell but not adjacent to any enemy currently. Lannister controls some near? Let's see Lannister's controlled regions: Harrenhal, Riverrun, Lannisport, the-golden-sound, port-of-lannisport. Not threatening white-harbor.

Greyjoy has pyke, ironmans-bay, port-of-pyke, greywater-watch.

Greywater-watch is adjacent to white-harbor via moats? Let's see map: "white-harbor [land; castle=1]: moat-cailin, port-of-white-harbor, the-narrow-sea, the-shivering-sea, widows-watch, winterfell". Not adjacent to greywater-watch (a different area). Greywater-watch is near Ironman's Bay.

Greyjoy can only get to white-harbor via ships crossing the Shivering Sea, then The Narrow Sea, then White Harbor? Actually ship transport: need ship units to connect sea areas. Greyjoy currently has a ship at Ironman's Bay; not adjacent.

Thus white-harbor seems safe.

Therefore, likely best move: discard the March order from white-harbor (no move). That leaves footman there, preserve castle, and preserve power token (no need to leave token). But also discarding the March order is possibly less beneficial than moving the ship from Shivering Sea to The Narrow Sea, which can provide ship transport later and maybe support. So we prioritize ship move.

Thus we will resolve the March order at "the-shivering-sea" moving ship (unit ID 4) to "the-narrow-sea". No combat, no power token needed. After that, we still have white-harbor March order pending for later decision, which we can decide later (stay or discard). Yes.

Check reachable region: "the-narrow-sea". That region currently has no units or order. The goal is to move the ship there.

We must ensure supply safe; moving a single ship is fine, supply unchanged.

Thus choose starting_region_id: "the-shivering-sea", moves list: one move entry with destination_region_id: "the-narrow-sea", unit_ids: [4] (since unit id 4 is ship). leave_power_token: false (since we are not vacating an area with castles, we are moving from a sea area; cannot assign token anyway). For the ship being moved from the-shivering-sea, vacated area is sea, no power token needed.

We must check that the actionGuide says "canLeavePowerToken": false for the-shivering-sea. Yes.

Thus produce JSON.

But we might also consider leaving power token? Not needed.

We must ensure we choose the correct unit ID: In board data, unit with id 4 is at the-shivering-sea, type "ship". Yes.

Thus final answer will be JSON object with fields as per schema.

Before final, maybe double-check check_neighbours for the-narrow-sea to confirm nothing there.

Let's call check_neighbours for "the-narrow-sea".

The-narrow-sea has no units, not owned, but has Shipbreaker Bay units (Baratheon) are present. Wait shipbreaker-bay is a sea area adjacent, has Baratheon ships (2). So moving the Stark ship into The Narrow Sea will place it adjacent to Baratheon's ships (shipbreaker-bay). That's okay.

Check if moving there triggers combat? In reachable info, "triggersCombat": false. Since it's moving into an empty sea area with only Baratheon ships in shipbreaker-bay, not same area. So no combat.

Now any issues of supply: moving ship alone, fine.

Thus final action: starting_region_id: "the-shivering-sea", moves: [{destination_region_id:"the-narrow-sea", unit_ids:[4]}], leave_power_token:false.

Make JSON accordingly.

But we also could optionally include the other March order later. But this decision only resolves one March order. So it's fine.

Let's double-check enumeration: starting_region_id enum values are "the-shivering-sea" or "white-harbor". Yes.

Check moves -> unit_ids: allowed ids 3,4. Since we are moving ship (id 4), okay.

Make final answer.

starting_region_id.description: Region containing the march order and moving units.
starting_region_id.title: Starting Region Id

moves.description: Destination groups and moving unit IDs. Unlisted units stay in the source. An empty list discards the order. Every group must be legal and fit Supply; an illegal final action is rejected without submitting the march.
moves.title: Moves

leave_power_token.description: Spend one available power token to preserve control when legally vacating the source area. This must be false if units remain or control cannot be established.
leave_power_token.title: Leave Power Token

actionOutputSchema.title: resolve_march_args
actionOutputSchema.description: You are resolving one of your March orders. You choose which remaining March area to resolve now. Choose which units move and their destinations. Units you omit remain in the source area; you may split an army across destinations, and a single unit can march on its own. An empty moves list removes this March order without moving anyone. Only one destination may start combat. Use the reachable destinations in actionGuidance and keep the resulting armies within Supply. Leaving a control token costs one available power token and preserves control of the source when you legally vacate it. Compare castles gained and lost, and count support around the destination battlefield before choosing an attack. Your final answer resolves this one order; another remaining order is a later decision.

We need to plan orders for Stark in round 5. The eligible regions are "bay-of-ice","castle-black","karhold","winterfell","the-narrow-sea". This is given in planningConstraints. Need to assign orders to each occupied area (all 5). Need to specify preferred_order, starred_preference, priority.

The restrictions: "restrictedOrderCategories":["raid"] and "restrictedStarredOrderCategories":["raid"]; that means we cannot assign Raid orders at all (restricted). Max starred orders: from planningConstraints, "maxStarredOrders":0. So we cannot use any starred orders this round.

Thus starred_preference must be "avoid". (But we still need to specify preference; they will allocate non-starred tokens if no starred tokens, which is fine).

We need to decide which orders to assign each area to (march, defense, support, consolidate_power). Also need to consider supply limit: Stark's supply is 1 (as per observation). Supply icons controlled: they have only winterfell (supply=1). So total supply track is 1. According to supply track table: Supply 1 permits armies: 3 and 2 (two armies: one max size 3, another max size 2). Actually from table: 1 => 3,2. So Stark can have up to 2 armies, sizes 3 and 2.

Current units and placement:

Based on board data:

- bay-of-ice: 1 ship (Stark)
- castle-black: 2 knights (Stark)
- karhold: 1 knight (Stark)
- winterfell: 1 footman (Stark)
- the-narrow-sea: 1 ship (Stark)

Thus we have 5 units (1 ship, 2 knights, 1 knight, 1 footman) = total 5. Check grouping:

- army is 2+ units in same land or sea area; a ship is a unit like any other.

Current groupings:

- bay-of-ice (sea) only ship (1 unit) -> not an army (single unit, doesn't count for supply). However supply counts armies (two+ units). Does a single unit not count? Yes.

- castle-black (land) knights count 2 units in same area -> This is an army of 2 knights (size 2). That's an army.

- karhold (land) 1 knight -> single unit, not an army.

- winterfell (land) 1 footman -> single unit.

- the-narrow-sea (sea) ship, single unit.

Thus currently the only army is the 2 knights at Castle Black (size 2). The other units are singles.

Supply track: Supply 1 permits: armies: 3, 2 (so can have up to 2 armies, one of up to 3 units, one up to 2 units). So currently we have 1 army (size 2). That's okay.

We can create a second army by moving a unit to join another unit. But cannot exceed supply: we can have at most 2 armies. So we should not create more than 2 armies (with total 5 units, we could make one army of 3 and one of 2, or one of 3 and others singles). But must not exceed allowed number of armies. Also an army is formed only when two or more units share the same area (land or sea). So if we move units, we must ensure we don't exceed limit.

Goal: expand to gain new castles. The text states: from Castle Black we can march to Flint's Finger. Actually Castle Black is adjacent to The Shivering Sea, not directly to Flint's Finger. But the description from "From Castle Black, the current land connections and friendly Ships reach these undefended castle areas you do not own: Flint's Finger." I think the path is via ship transport? Castle Black (land area) has adjacent sea the Shivering Sea; the Stark ship at The Narrow Sea might be used to transport via ship? Let's examine connections.

We need to check map: 

- castle-black is a land area that neighbors: bay-of-ice, karhold, the-shivering-sea, winterfell.
- The Shivering Sea is a sea area adjacent to castle-black, also adjacent to karhold, the-narrow-sea, white-harbor, widows-watch, winterfell. There's a ship at the narrow sea (Stark ship). Possibly we could move that ship to The Shivering Sea via normal sea movement (ship moving from a sea area to adjacent sea area, with a March order). Then with ship transport, can move knights from Castle Black across the ship to some other coastal area.

Flint's Finger is a land area; we need to see its adjacency: flints-finger [land; castle=1]: neighbors: bay-of-ice, greywater-watch, ironmans-bay, sunset-sea. So to reach Flint's Finger, we need to move via Bay of Ice (sea) and maybe ships. We have a ship at bay-of-ice already.

From Winterfell, you can also march to Flint's Finger, Moat Cailin, White Harbor. Those are reachable via ships? Let's see Winterfell neighbors: bay-of-ice, castle-black, karhold, moat-cailin, port-of-winterfell, the-shivering-sea, the-stony-shore, white-harbor.

Winterfell is adjacent to bay-of-ice (sea) and white-harbor (land) and moat-cailin (land). Both contain castle=1? Moat Cailin is a castle. White Harbor has a castle (castle=1). Flint's Finger reachable via bay-of-ice (sea) then maybe a ship to flints-finger? Actually flints-finger has adjacency to bay-of-ice (sea). Bay-of-ice is a sea area; flints-finger is a land area that is adjacent to bay-of-ice (i.e., you could march from Bay-of-Ice (sea) to flints-finger? Ship can move onto land if it's a port? No, ship units cannot march onto land area, only footmen etc. Ships can transport other units across sea but to land they need a port adjacency: ports are separate area connected to land but only ships can be in ports. So to move a land unit (knight or footman) to Flint's Finger, you need a Ship in adjacent sea area (like bay-of-ice or ironmans-bay) and use Ship transport rule: A land unit can march from a coastal area to another coastal area if there is a line of adjoining sea areas (with ships) connecting them. For example, a knight at Winterfell could be in a coastal area? Winterfell is a land with a coast? Based on map it's an inland area? However it borders bay-of-ice (sea) and the-shivering-sea; that indicates it's coastal. So knights at Winterfell can march to a land area like Flint's Finger if there is a chain of sea areas each containing at least one friendly Ship connecting Winterfell's adjacent sea to the destination's adjacent sea. Equivalent: Ship transport: two land areas are adjacent if they are connected by consecutive sea areas each containing friendly ships (they can be the same ship used as a bridge). So if Stark has a ship at Bay-of-Ice, and that is adjacent to both Winterfell and Flint's Finger, that could suffice to move from Winterfell to Flint's Finger in a single March order (through the ship). However for Ship transport you need the ship to be placed in the sea area (bay-of-ice). The shore for Flint's Finger is adjacent to bay-of-ice (sea). So yes, a unit in a land area adjacent to bay-of-ice (Winterfell) can move to Flint's Finger using ship transport via the ship in bay-of-ice.

Given Stark currently has the ship at bay-of-ice. So we have a ship in Bay-of-Ice.

Thus a March order from Winterfell (or Castle Black or other area connected to Bay-of-Ice using ship transport) could target Flint's Finger or Moat Cailin or White Harbor. However to move to Moat Cailin (land area, castle=1) it is directly adjacent to Winterfell (land). So a direct march from Winterfell to Moat Cailin is possible (land adjacency). That would be moving a single footman onto Moat Cailin.

But moving a single unit from Winterfell will vacate Winterfell, but the home area provides a "home area" control automatically (it's the home area). According to rule: Home area control is automatically maintained; you can vacate Winterfell without needing a power token. However, you lose the castle control (but you still control via home area? Actually Winterfell has a castle (castle=2 stronghold) which counts for victory points. According to rules, the home area is considered controlled automatically, meaning the printed shield functions like a Power token that cannot be removed, and you can control it even if vacant. It says "From the beginning of the game, a House is considered to have established control of its own home area, meaning the printed House shield functions like a Power token that cannot be removed." So even if you vacate Winterfell, you still have control of the area (and the castle). So moving a unit out does not lose the castle.

Thus you can try to march from Winterfell to Moat Cailin (castle) capturing it. That would be an expansion. Alternatively, marching from Castle Black to Flint's Finger also captures a castle.

We also have a ship at the narrow sea. The narrow sea adjacent to castle-black, karhold, winterfell, etc. Could use for transport elsewhere.

Now we need to decide orders. Max starred orders = 0. So all orders must be regular (non-starred). There are a limited number of each order token. From orderLegend:

'1': "March -1" (regular)
'2': "March +0" (regular)
'3': "March +1" (special? Actually legendary: March +1 is special (starred?) The orderLegend mapping shows 1-3 are March orders: -1, +0, +1. But likely March +1 is the Special March order (starred). The count of special orders = number of stars on King’s Court. From strategic overview: Max starred orders = 0. Means we cannot use any special orders (including March +1, Defense +2, Support +1, Raid special, Consolidate Power starred). So we must only use regular March -1 (order id 1), March +0 (id2) maybe both are regular. However we also only have limited number of March orders: each player has 2 normal March orders (one -1, one +0). So we can assign at most two March orders across the 5 areas. May need to prioritize.

We cannot assign more than one order per area. Must assign an order token to each area containing at least one unit. So we must assign 5 orders (in 5 regions). Some will be optionally March, Defense, Support, Consolidate Power. But we have restrictions on categories: raid restricted, but not others. So ok.

Now determine which order types to assign:

Key issue: we have 5 units across 5 areas, each area with a unit (or multiple units for castle-black). For building a march, we want to attempt to capture new castles. There are 3 possible target castles reachable:

- Flint's Finger (from Castle Black or Winterfell via ship)
- Moat Cailin (adjacent to Winterfell)
- White Harbor (adjacent to Winterfell)
- Possibly also any others reachable from other areas.

We have only two March orders available. So we can only attempt two moves in this round.

Which are high priority? Probably capture Moat Cailin or Flint's Finger. Need to consider supply and leaving castles unprotected. Castle Black contains 2 knights (army). If we assign March from Castle Black (using March -1 or +0) to move some or all units, we must ensure supply constraints after moving. If we move both knights away, Castle Black would lose its army (and then not have any units). However, a castle area that has no units still is controlled by the player if we have a power token? Actually a Castle area provides control if you have units there; if you vacate it you lose control unless you place a power token. However the rule: When you vacate a land area (all units leave), you may place a power token to preserve control. If you leave a castle area empty and don't place a power token, you lose control of that castle, losing a victory point.

Thus moving both knights from Castle Black would cause us to lose the castle if we cannot place a power token (we have 3 power tokens available). We could place a power token to hold Castle Black. But we have only 3 power tokens in total (as per house data). However we need to maintain power tokens usage for other areas maybe. We currently have power tokens placed in some areas: At castle-black none, karhold none, winterfell none, bay-of-ice none, the-narrow-sea none. So we have 3 power tokens available (but we have a total of 3 tokens). We could place a power token in Castle Black if we march both knights out, but that would use all tokens (or some). Might be okay but we need to consider if we need to hold other areas later.

Alternatively, we could keep at least one unit at Castle Black, and move one knight to somewhere else. That would still keep control of the castle (because there will still be a unit there). We could also move the footman from Winterfell while still leaving the castle? Actually Winterfell is home area; we can vacate without token.

Thus best to use March orders from Winterfell and Castle Black perhaps: Use March from Winterfell to Moat Cailin or White Harbor; use March from Castle Black to Flint's Finger. However we need to consider supply constraints. If we move footman from Winterfell to Moat Cailin, we would have two knights still at Castle Black (army size 2) and one footman at Moat Cailin (single unit). Supply remains okay: we have one army size 2, and a single unit, fine.

If we also move a knight from Castle Black to Flint's Finger, we'd have one knight left at Castle Black (single unit), which would break the army concept (single unit does not count as army). So after that move we would have 0 armies (both knights are singles). Actually there would be no area with two units. That means we would have zero armies, which is allowed as supply allows up to 2 armies but we can have fewer. That's fine. However the March order taking a knight from Castle Black to Flint's Finger will create a new single unit at Flint's Finger (just the knight). That is okay. Supply wise we have only one army (none actually). But we have a single unit at Castle Black (still controls the castle). So no supply violation.

Thus moving a single knight from Castle Black to Flint's Finger via ship transport could be feasible.

Alternatively, we could assign a Defense order at Castle Black to protect it, but we aren't expecting combat now. Might be less useful.

We also have other areas: Karhold (Knight) alone; Bay-of-Ice (Ship); The Narrow Sea (Ship). We need to assign orders to those areas too; we could set Consolidate Power there to earn power – for bay-of-ice? It's a sea area, Consolidate Power yields no power (except there may be a power icon in the area; but bay-of-ice is sea (no power icon). So Consolidate Power at sea yields only the base token (1 token). Actually "Consolidate Power Orders ... when resolved, the Order token is removed from the game board in exchange for gaining one Power token from the Power Pool, plus one Power token for each Power icon printed on the assigned area." So you get at least 1 token from the order itself. So it's useful to get power.

But maybe we want to preserve supply for future moves. The ship at Bay-of-Ice if we assign Consolidate Power there, we will get 1 power token (since no power icon). Same for The Narrow Sea.

But we could also assign Defense or Support orders on Karhold or Bay-of-Ice to bolster potential upcoming combats (if opponents attack). But no immediate threat known.

We need to allocate orders based on priority: assign high priority March orders attempts for expansion.

We have 5 areas; we can assign:

1. winterfell: March (to Moat Cailin or White Harbor) – we need to decide which target is reachable and beneficial. Both Moat Cailin (castle=1) and White Harbor (castle=1) are potential castles to capture. Which is better? White Harbor is adjacent to winterfell; Moat Cailin also adjacent. Both have castles. White Harbor also connects to port? It is a land area with a port (port-of-white-harbor) adjacent (sea). But probably similar. Let's check control situation: currently Moat Cailin is controlled by Greyjoy (controlPowerToken is "greyjoy"). Actually board data shows "moat-cailin [land; castle=1]: controlPowerToken": "greyjoy". That means Greyjoy placed a power token there. But they do have a unit? Actually moat-cailin has no units (units list empty). So Greyjoy controls Moat Cailin by power token.

To capture Moat Cailin, we would need to move a unit into it; if it's unoccupied, we can just move in and take control (capture) without combat (since no enemy units). However, there is a power token there; when a unit moves into an area containing only an opponent’s Power token (and no enemy units), it does not result in combat, and the Power token is simply discarded to the Power Pool. So you can capture it by moving a unit there. So moving footman there will automatically remove Greyjoy’s power token and gain control. That's good.

But need to check that Greyjoy has a power token on Moat Cailin; they have 8 total power tokens, so they could be placed elsewhere. So taking Moat Cailin maybe reduces Greyjoy's power.

Similarly White Harbor is a castle, but with no control token. It's empty of units; no power token is there. If we move there, we capture it.

Which is better? Moat Cailin is also a strategic gateway to the north (connected to winterfell, white-harbor, etc) and provides a castle. White Harbor also leads to another port.

Given we might also want to preserve ship positions, we may choose White Harbor or Moat Cailin. I'd incline to pick Moat Cailin because it's already held by Greyjoy; capturing it both expands and denies them a power token. White Harbor also useful but perhaps less immediate.

Thus choose March from Winterfell to Moat Cailin (or White Harbor). We'll need to note target? In order assignment, we just specify preferred_order "march". The harness will allocate a March order token (either -1 or +0). The star preference is avoid.

Next, castle-black: March (to Flint's Finger). Use March to capture Flints-Finger.

However, moving a knight from Castle Black to Flint's Finger may create a new single unit at Flint's Finger, but we might consider need for ship transport. The route: Castle Black adjacent to Bay-of-Ice (sea). We have a ship at Bay-of-Ice. So we can move knight using ship transport. That counts as movement into Flint's Finger (land). That's legal.

Thus assign March on Castle Black.

Now Karhold: what order? Could be Support, Defense, Consolidate Power. There's a knight there. Could assign Support to aid either of the March attacks (the one from Castle Black or Winterfell). For supporting, support orders can be used by adjacent area to embattled area (but these are not engaged in combat yet). But later, in combat they can support the attacker or defender. Since we're planning to attack at Flint's Finger and Moat Cailin, which are not adjacent to Karhold or to Castle Black? Let's examine adjacency:

- Karhold is adjacent to Castle Black, The Shivering Sea, Winterfell. So Karhold seems adjacent to Winterfell (land). So a Support order placed at Karhold can support an attack on an adjacent area. But the combat hasn't happened yet. Later, when Winterfell attacks Moat Cailin (adjacent), the support could come from Karhold (if it's adjacent to Moat Cailin?). Let's check adjacency: Moat Cailin neighbors: greywater-watch, seagard, the-narrow-sea, the-twins, white-harbor, winterfell. Karhold is not adjacent to Moat Cailin directly. So Karhold cannot support an attack on Moat Cailin. However Support can be placed in any area adjacent to the embattled area, not to the attacking area necessarily. So Karhold cannot support Moat Cailin attack. Could support an attack on Castle Black? If we have March from Castle Black to Flint's Finger, the embattled area would be Flint's Finger. Which areas are adjacent to Flint's Finger? Adjacent to flints-finger: bay-of-ice, greywater-watch, ironmans-bay, sunset-sea. Karhold is not adjacent to them, so cannot support. actionOutputSchema.description: You are placing planning orders for this round. Assign an order preference to each required occupied area, respecting the displayed restrictions and starred-order limit. Your final answer submits the whole order draft and marks your house ready. These orders determine what your armies can do later; this decision does not move units. A single land unit can capture an empty castle with a March order. Defence and Support orders do not move that unit or claim neighbouring land. Consolidate Power in an open sea earns no power; a port follows the separate port rule. The harness allocates the physical order tokens, preserving higher-priority preferences when not all requested categories fit the available tokens. Priority 100 is most important; 0 is least important. Plan how to gain castle areas this round. Use Defence or Support when you have a concrete battle to protect or assist; otherwise these orders can leave an army unable to expand.
